title: Turn overlapping windows into modes
summary: SSA decomposes a lag matrix and maps its grouped modes back to time-domain components.

steps.title: Embed overlapping windows
steps.text: Slide an L-sample window across the series. Put each window in a column. Repeated observations lie on anti-diagonals, which is the Hankel structure used by SSA.

steps.title: Factor the trajectory matrix
steps.text: Compute X = U diag(s) V^T. Each singular triplet gives one rank-one matrix. Retaining only a chosen number of modes determines which matrix structure can enter subsequent grouping.

steps.title: Average each anti-diagonal
steps.text: A rank-one matrix need not itself be Hankel. Average its anti-diagonals to turn its repeated time-index estimates back into one time-domain reconstructed component.

steps.title: Group trend and season
steps.text: This example uses DeTime's primary-period frequency heuristic. Low-frequency modes are assigned to trend and modes near 1/period to season, with documented fallbacks if a group is empty. Residual is the observed input minus those two groups. Explicit component-index lists can replace this automatic grouping.

parameters.name: window
parameters.effect: Embedding length L; changes the temporal scale and matrix dimensions.

parameters.name: rank
parameters.effect: Number of singular modes available for grouping; more modes can retain both signal structure and noise.

parameters.name: primary_period
parameters.effect: Target period for the frequency-based seasonal grouping heuristic.

parameters.name: trend_components / season_components
parameters.effect: Optional zero-based mode indices that explicitly define the groups.

parameters.name: season_freq_tol_ratio / trend_freq_threshold
parameters.effect: Control the frequency bands used by automatic grouping.

cautions: The labels trend and season come from a grouping rule; singular-value order alone does not establish physical meaning.
Changing window, rank, or grouping can change components even when additive reconstruction remains exact.
The animation uses backend='python', speed_mode='exact'. Native or randomized fast paths are separate numerical execution choices.
This is an offline decomposition. Forecasting features must be recomputed using only observations available at each forecast origin.

references.title: Golyandina and Zhigljavsky (2020), Singular Spectrum Analysis for Time Series

trace_note: The trajectory matrix, exact SVD, reconstructed modes, and grouped outputs are computed from the source algorithm. Checks compare trace modes and final groups with the configured Python implementation. The animation explains construction order, not solver wall-clock execution.
input_note: Deterministic synthetic teaching signal; not a benchmark.
